requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain four features of the free enterprise system in the United States. Describe the difference between freedom and license. Tell how the Scout Oath and Scout Law apply to business and free enterprise. (b) Describe the Industrial Revolution and tell about the major developments that marked the start of the modern industrial era in the United States. Discuss three people who had a great influence on business or industry in the United States and describe what each did. (c) Identify and describe to your counselor the five primary areas of business. (d) Explain the history of labor unions in the United States and the importance of labor unions and employers working together. Identify two major labor unions currently in existence. (e) Discuss with your counselor how business impacts the local, national, and global economy.

pamphlet_excerpts: Andmany Others Wanted: He andmany others wanted the United States, which had won itsindependence from Great Britain just a few years earlier, tobecome economically strong.
They Organized: They organized associationsthat promoted industrialization.
Than Three-fourths: Although more than three-fourths of the workingpopulation in the United States was involved in agriculture atthe time, the Industrial Revolution spread.
End Century United: By the end of the century, the United Statesbecame the world leader in manufacturing and spurred what isknown as the Second Industrial Revolution.
step_by_step_procedure: United Statescontinues: The United Statescontinues to be one of the world's largest producers of goods.
Result Globalization: The result of globalization is a worldeconomy in which the borders between countries have blurred.
Technology Internet Helped: Technology, such as the internet, has helped makeglobal corporations and m ­ arkets possible.
Globalization Grown Rapidly: Globalization has grown rapidly since the 1970s, but it hasbeen an economic trend since the end of World War II in 1945.

pamphlet_excerpts: Business Contracts Formal: Many business contracts are formal and complicated.
Other contracts Informal: Other contracts are informal and hardly noticeable.
Business Transaction Simple: Every business transaction, from one as simple asbuying a snack to one as complex as a company issuing stock, is a contract of some type.
Partytrusts She Promised: Each partytrusts the other to do what he or she has promised.
step_by_step_procedure: Financial Statements: Financial statements for businesses usually include incomestatements, balance sheets, statements of retained earnings, andstatements of cash flows.
Financialstatements Audited: Financialstatements are often audited by government agencies, accountants, firms, and other entities to ensure accuracy and for tax.
Main Financialstatements: The three main financialstatements are the balance sheet, income statement, and cashflow statement.
Balance Sheet Provides: The balance sheet provides an overview of assets, liabilities, andshareholders’ equity as a snapshot in time.
